title: Uber Real-Time Marketplace
summary: How marketplace events feed low-latency analytics, lakehouse data, and ML decisions.

nodes.label: Marketplace events
nodes.description: Trips, GPS, rider demand, driver supply, Eats orders, and service logs.

nodes.label: Kafka topics
nodes.description: Thousands of services publish data for real-time and offline consumers.

nodes.label: FlinkSQL transforms
nodes.description: Streaming SQL filters, joins, and pre-aggregates data before serving.

nodes.label: Pinot OLAP
nodes.description: Fresh analytical tables serve dashboards and product-facing queries.

nodes.label: Hudi data lake
nodes.description: Incremental tables preserve large histories for analytics and ML.

nodes.label: Michelangelo
nodes.description: The ML platform trains, deploys, serves, and monitors production models.

nodes.label: Marketplace decisions
nodes.description: ETA, fraud, matching, routing, and pricing decisions affect the live market.

steps.title: Capture market state
steps.description: The marketplace only works if supply, demand, and movement data are visible quickly enough to act on.

steps.title: Prepare real-time tables
steps.description: FlinkSQL jobs transform Kafka streams into shapes that Pinot can query with low latency.

steps.title: Preserve correction-friendly history
steps.description: A Hudi-backed lake keeps incremental history available when analytics and ML need more than live streams.

steps.title: Train and serve models
steps.description: Michelangelo uses historical and fresh features to deploy models for ETA, fraud, and marketplace decisions.

steps.title: Operate the live loop
steps.description: Dashboards and predictions change the marketplace, then those changes create new data to measure.
